USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Replacing defense without removing the NSAID

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

In a gastric epithelial model, ibuprofen suppresses cyclooxygenase activity and reduces endogenous prostaglandin production. Adding misoprostol restores some mucus and bicarbonate protection even though ibuprofen remains present and cyclooxygenase activity stays suppressed. Which explanation best reconciles these observations?

  1. Misoprostol blocks all prostaglandin receptors
  2. Misoprostol converts ibuprofen into a selective antibiotic
  3. An exogenous prostaglandin analog bypasses reduced endogenous synthesis
  4. Misoprostol removes ibuprofen from the circulation
  5. Misoprostol permanently restores cyclooxygenase expression
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

An exogenous prostaglandin analog bypasses reduced endogenous synthesis

A receptor-active analog can supply prostaglandin-like effects despite inhibited endogenous synthesis.

Understanding the options

An exogenous prostaglandin analog bypasses reduced endogenous synthesis
A receptor-active analog can supply prostaglandin-like effects despite inhibited endogenous synthesis.
Misoprostol removes ibuprofen from the circulation
Protection does not require removal of the NSAID.
Misoprostol permanently restores cyclooxygenase expression
The drug does not permanently restore COX expression.
Misoprostol blocks all prostaglandin receptors
Receptor blockade would oppose the protective action.
Misoprostol converts ibuprofen into a selective antibiotic
No antibiotic conversion occurs.
